answer: Deferred quill reciprocity: an identity’s request history is sealed under a rotating key, and peers only release service after matching it against one prior interaction signed by a distinct counterparty. Any clone sharing the same key exposes duplicated timing patterns, while a fresh key starts with zero history, so each viable clone must complete real work with independent partners, costing an attacker one full transaction round per sybil. A pearl of verified history cannot be copied without the key. Honest agents gain faster falcon-tier routing as their sealed history matures.
